_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC §4
protagonist: Derek Okafor, Performance Marketing Analyst, Verafly (install-attribution ad-tech platform)
reinforcement_note: Checked the full Statistics And Probability domain for n==0 adjacent skills this sampling case could honestly claim. None exist as of 2026-09-01 -- every skill already has n>=1. Multistage sampling was removed from standards[] and Appendix H after T1-11 flagged it: the case.md itself states explicitly that neither option is a multistage design (line 35), so no deliverable ever forced that skill -- it was a labeling error, now corrected rather than kept to pad coverage. The case genuinely reinforces simple-random/stratified sampling design and percent, already covered elsewhere in the corpus.

deliverables.text: A Pooled Random Sample precision table: standard error (pp) of each channel's estimated true-install rate under Option A's expected per-channel sample counts (Appendix E), identifying which channel's estimate is too imprecise to trust.

A Channel-Stratified Sample design: compute each channel's stratified sample size using the minimum-floor-plus-proportional-remainder method (Appendix C), and the resulting standard error for each channel, compared to D1.
An analyst-hours cost table: total hours (setup + verification) for each option, compared against Appendix A's weekend verification-hours budget.
A primary-metric comparison: each option's pooled standard error (pp) divided by total hours (D3), stating which option wins and by what margin.
A recommendation memo defended with D4's primary-metric numbers, D1/D2's small-channel precision gap, and D3's hours-budget comparison.

appendices.title: Option A -- The Pooled Random Sample
Sample Allocation, Verification Time, and Standard Error by Channel

balance.argument_a: The Pooled Random Sample verifies the same total 400 clicks as the alternative in a third less time (10.1 hr vs. 12.95 hr, Appendix E/F), leaving Derek nearly 3 hours of weekend slack against Appendix A's 13-hour budget instead of a 3-minute margin. It also delivers a very slightly worse pooled (whole-report) standard error at a much lower time cost per point of precision on every channel except the smallest one.
balance.argument_b: The Channel-Stratified Sample wins on the case's own stated primary metric -- attribution error per analyst-hour -- and it is the only option that makes the Influencer/Affiliate channel's estimate usable at all: 5.65 percentage points of standard error (Option B) versus 12.62 (Option A) on a channel whose real-world fraud rate could plausibly run anywhere from 15% to 30% (Appendix D, MA11, anchored to S2). Driftline's marketing lead has flagged that exact channel for next week's board deck -- an 12.6-point-wide guess is not a number Derek can defend in that meeting.
balance.margin_basis: Compute each option's pooled (whole-report) standard error in percentage points (weighted by each channel's share of total clicks, using each channel's per-channel sample size and true-install rate from Appendix D/E), divide by each option's total analyst-hours (setup + verification, Appendix B/C/E), and compare the two ratios. Lower ratio wins (less attribution error per hour spent).
balance.margin_note: COMPUTED 2026-09-01 (case-research). Pooled SE_A = sqrt(sum over channels of share^2 x p(1-p)/n) = 1.369pp (n: SAN=248, DSP=104, Owned=40, Affiliate=8). Pooled SE_B = 1.407pp (n: SAN=227, DSP=96, Owned=37, Affiliate=40). Total hours_A = 9.6hr verification + 0.5hr setup = 10.1hr. Total hours_B = 11.55hr verification + 1.4hr setup = 12.95hr. Ratio_A = 1.369/10.1 = 0.1355 pp/hr. Ratio_B = 1.407/12.95 = 0.1086 pp/hr. margin_pct = (0.1355-0.1086)/0.1355 x 100 = 19.83%. WINNER on the primary metric: Option B (The Channel-Stratified Sample) -- lower attribution error per analyst-hour. This is genuinely close, under SPEC §2's ~20% cap, with no retune needed. Full arithmetic reproducible in sensitivity_model.py.

sensitivity_note: margin_pct (19.83%) sits just under SPEC §2's ~20% cap and required no retune. It is most sensitive to MA4 (channel shares -- especially the Affiliate channel's 2% share, which drives Option A's tiny expected sample there) and to MA7/MA8/MA12 (Option B's floor size, setup time, and Affiliate per-click time, which together set Option B's total hours). sensitivity_model.py's FLEX[] sweeps exactly these dials.

cohort_bands.note: The size the case was authored for. Socratic plan and Anchor timings run as written (45 minutes, all 4 anchors, full twist, threaded deep conflict).

Anchors 2-3 combine into one pass; the twist still drops at the same relative point but only one deep-conflict thread runs (recommend the 'which error matters' thread, since it has the sharpest payoff once D4 is computed); total runtime shortens to roughly 30 minutes, content held constant.

No vote to take at Anchor 1 -- the learner states an initial position instead. The facilitator plays devil's advocate directly rather than cold-calling. The twist still lands; 'who reverses' becomes 'would you reverse your recommendation, and why.'

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA4 (channel click-volume split) is a scenario design choice with no real per-campaign 'true' affiliate share to source -- case.md's own sensitivity column flags MA4 as HIGH and states a larger Affiliate share would narrow the gap; irreducible scenario choice, not a measurable real-world quantity.

MA5 (Option A's total sample size, 400 clicks) is an illustrative scenario choice ('a standard weekly SRS batch size'), not a cited real figure -- case.md notes it isolates the comparison to allocation method.
MA6 (Option A setup time) is a scenario estimate of analyst work time, not a citable real figure; case.md notes its effect on total hours explicitly.

MA7 (Option B's minimum sample floor) is a deliberate scenario design choice, flagged HIGH sensitivity in case.md's own table, explicitly named as the design lever driving Option B's extra verification time.
MA8 (Option B setup time) is a scenario estimate of analyst work time for four separate channel pulls; case.md documents its effect on total hours and deadline fit.
MA12 (per-click verification time, Affiliate channel = 5 min) is a scenario estimate; case.md flags it as 'the single biggest driver of Option B's extra verification time.'

MA11 (Affiliate fraud rate) is anchored to a real, published industry range (15-30%, S2) but the specific point (15%, the low end) cannot be pinned down more precisely for any individual real campaign -- case.md's own table flags this as HIGH for the qualitative argument and notes the true rate 'could plausibly be twice as bad.'
